short: The night in November 1989 when the Cold War's most physical symbol was opened.
full:
The Wall had divided Berlin since 1961, and at least 140 people died trying to cross it. By late 1989 East Germany was losing citizens through Hungary and Czechoslovakia faster than it could govern, and mass demonstrations in Leipzig had gone unsuppressed.

On the evening of 9 November a Politburo spokesman, reading a hastily drafted note on relaxed travel rules, was asked when it took effect and answered — apparently in error — 'immediately, without delay'. Crowds gathered at the checkpoints, the overwhelmed guards eventually opened them, and people crossed freely for the first time in twenty-eight years. Germany was formally reunified within a year, and the Soviet Union dissolved two years later.
